CREATIVE ARTS — MOCK EXAM #5
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is the correct order for making charcoal sticks? (1 mark)
   A. Cut, trim, burn, cool
   B. Burn, cut, trim, cool
   C. Cool, burn, trim, cut
   D. Trim, cool, burn, cut

2. Which players are allowed to shoot at goal? (1 mark)
   A. Only C
   B. WA and WD
   C. GS and GA
   D. GK and GD

3. Which is a good safety rule before playing netball? (1 mark)
   A. Play with long sharp nails
   B. Play on broken ground
   C. Remove rings and bracelets
   D. Wear a necklace

4. Which is true about netball skills? (1 mark)
   A. Nobody needs to move
   B. Passing and catching are needed by every player
   C. Only the umpire needs to pass
   D. Only shooters need to catch

5. Why is colour classification useful in painting? (1 mark)
   A. It cleans the brush
   B. It makes paint cheaper
   C. It makes paper thicker
   D. It tells us which colours to mix to make others

6. Which colours are the primary colours? (1 mark)
   A. Red, yellow and blue
   B. Orange, green and purple
   C. Black, white and grey
   D. Red, green and brown

7. How many guide lines are used for practising lettering in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Ten
   B. Two
   C. Four
   D. Six

8. In ta-te taa taa (rest), how many beats are there? (1 mark)
   A. Four
   B. Two
   C. Three
   D. Five

9. Which letter has a descender? (1 mark)
   A. k
   B. g
   C. a
   D. e

10. Which is the lowest of the notes d, r and m? (1 mark)
   A. They are all the same
   B. d
   C. r
   D. m

11. Which describes a false start in a sprint? (1 mark)
   A. Falling at the end
   B. Running in the wrong direction
   C. Finishing first
   D. Moving before the last signal

12. Which foot is usually placed in front at the start? (1 mark)
   A. The weaker foot always
   B. The stronger foot, used to kick a ball
   C. Both together
   D. Neither

13. How far apart are the hands placed at the start? (1 mark)
   A. Shoulder-width apart
   B. Touching each other
   C. As far as possible
   D. One on each side of the track

14. In a partner check for the crab balance, how many touching points does the table have? (1 mark)
   A. Eight
   B. Two
   C. Six
   D. Four

15. A roll in gymnastics is (1 mark)
   A. a run
   B. a movement in which the body turns over along the floor
   C. a still position
   D. a song

16. What is the last part of the sequence in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Getting up slowly and standing tall
   B. Running away
   C. Jumping
   D. Rolling backwards

17. Which folk songs welcome a new baby? (1 mark)
   A. Initiation songs
   B. Naming songs
   C. Funeral songs
   D. Work songs

18. Which facial expression fits a joyful song? (1 mark)
   A. A yawn
   B. Closed eyes
   C. A smile
   D. A frown

19. A sign that gets wider to the right means (1 mark)
   A. getting louder
   B. getting softer
   C. stop
   D. slow

20. What does good diction mean? (1 mark)
   A. Clapping
   B. Singing with no words
   C. Saying the words clearly
   D. Singing very loudly

21. Who should you ask before using a school digital device? (1 mark)
   A. Nobody
   B. A stranger
   C. A friend's pet
   D. A teacher or adult

22. On the staff, the note B sits on (1 mark)
   A. line 1
   B. line 2
   C. line 5
   D. line 3

23. When you make a mistake while playing in a group, you should (1 mark)
   A. shout
   B. carry on with the beat
   C. throw your recorder
   D. stop the whole group

24. Of the notes B, A and G, which is the lowest? (1 mark)
   A. A
   B. B
   C. G
   D. They are equal

25. Which note is played with the thumb and holes 1, 2 and 3 covered? (1 mark)
   A. A
   B. B
   C. G
   D. F

26. What should you do before playing to prevent spreading germs? (1 mark)
   A. Wash your hands
   B. Eat sweets
   C. Chew gum
   D. Share the recorder

27. Floating means (1 mark)
   A. staying on top of the water without swimming
   B. diving
   C. swimming fast
   D. sinking

28. When playing an animal game, you should play on (1 mark)
   A. thorn bushes
   B. broken glass
   C. soft, clear ground
   D. sharp stones

29. In a folk song, the soloist (1 mark)
   A. leads and sings the call
   B. is the audience
   C. is silent
   D. plays the drum only

30. The message of an art work is (1 mark)
   A. what the artist wants us to learn or feel
   B. the size of the frame
   C. the price
   D. the artist's age

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. How should you give feedback on a friend's photograph? (3 marks)

32. Describe how to learn the East African Community anthem for performance. (4 marks)

33. How should you receive feedback from others? (3 marks)

34. What is the difference between tempo and dynamics? (2 marks)

35. State how many finger holes a descant recorder has in front and where the thumb hole is. (2 marks)

36. Explain how to write a rhythm from dictation. (3 marks)

37. Name the three primary colours. (2 marks)

38. Describe the sit-and-slide water entry. (3 marks)

39. Give four safety rules for sprint races. (4 marks)

40. Explain how you decide whether a percussion instrument is melodic or non-melodic. (3 marks)

41. Write the rhythm names of a pattern of a crotchet, a crotchet rest, a pair of quavers and a crotchet. (3 marks)

42. Describe three qualities of a good rhythmic pattern. (3 marks)

43. State what the colours black and green stand for on the Kenyan flag. (2 marks)

44. State three ways of showing fair play in a netball game. (3 marks)

45. Explain how good singing performance is achieved, using posture, breathing, diction, expression and etiquette. (5 marks)

46. Describe how to make an overhead pass. (3 marks)

47. Write what the signs p and f mean. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — MOCK EXAM #5 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Cut, trim, burn, cool
   The stages are cutting, trimming, burning, then cooling.

2. C — GS and GA
   Only the Goal Shooter and the Goal Attack may score.

3. C — Remove rings and bracelets
   Jewellery can hurt you and others.

4. B — Passing and catching are needed by every player
   Every player passes and catches during a game.

5. D — It tells us which colours to mix to make others
   Knowing primary and secondary colours helps us mix what we need.

6. A — Red, yellow and blue
   Primary colours cannot be made by mixing other colours.

7. C — Four
   Ascender line, top of small letters, baseline and descender line make four.

8. A — Four
   Each of ta-te, taa, taa and the rest fills one beat, so there are four beats.

9. B — g
   The tail of g goes below the baseline.

10. B — d
   Doh is the lowest of the three.

11. D — Moving before the last signal
   A false start is leaving before the start signal.

12. B — The stronger foot, used to kick a ball
   The stronger foot is the front foot.

13. A — Shoulder-width apart
   Hands are about shoulder-width apart.

14. D — Four
   The table has four legs, two hands and two feet.

15. B — a movement in which the body turns over along the floor
   A roll turns the body over along the mat.

16. A — Getting up slowly and standing tall
   Finish by standing up slowly with control.

17. B — Naming songs
   Naming songs are sung when a baby is named.

18. C — A smile
   Facial expressions show the mood.

19. A — getting louder
   An opening sign means the music grows louder.

20. C — Saying the words clearly
   Clear words help the audience understand the message.

21. D — A teacher or adult
   Always get permission.

22. D — line 3
   B is on the middle line.

23. B — carry on with the beat
   Continue and rejoin.

24. C — G
   More holes covered gives a lower note.

25. C — G
   G adds the third hole.

26. A — Wash your hands
   Clean hands help hygiene.

27. A — staying on top of the water without swimming
   Floating is resting on the surface.

28. C — soft, clear ground
   Soft, clear ground prevents injuries.

29. A — leads and sings the call
   The soloist starts or leads.

30. A — what the artist wants us to learn or feel
   The message is the idea communicated.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: Say what you like first, comment on light and centre of interest, and suggest one improvement politely.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: Listen to it several times, read and discuss the words, clap the rhythm, sing line by line and then sing the whole song together in unison while standing straight and respectful.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: Listen quietly, do not argue, say thank you and think about the ideas.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: Tempo is the speed of the music. Dynamics are how loud or soft the music is.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: Seven finger holes in front and the thumb hole is at the back.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: Listen twice to the pattern. Count the beats. For each beat decide if it was one long sound, two short sounds or silence, and write taa, ta-te or a rest.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: Red, yellow and blue.
   Working / marking points: Award 2 marks for all three, 1 mark for two.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sit on the edge with feet in the water, hands on the edge beside the hips. Turn to face the wall and slide gently into the water holding the edge.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: Run in your own lane; check the track for stones; wear proper clothes; never push or trip; slow down gradually after the finish; warm up. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Listen to the sounds. If it plays different notes, high and low, that make a tune, it is melodic. If it gives only a beat or one kind of sound, it is non-melodic.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for listening, 1 mark for melodic meaning, 1 mark for non-melodic meaning.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: taa (rest) ta-te taa
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct part in order.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: It has variation of note values, repetition of a group of notes and ends on a long note.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: Black stands for the people of Kenya. Green stands for the land and its natural wealth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Follow the rules; respect the umpire; shake hands with the other team; take turns in positions; encourage teammates. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

45. (5 marks)
   Answer: Stand tall with a relaxed body. Breathe deeply and sing on the breath. Say the words clearly. Use gestures and facial expressions to show the message and mood. Walk on and off quietly and respect others.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of five points.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Lift the ball above the head with both hands and elbows slightly bent. Step forward and throw from behind the head, flicking wrists and fingers so the ball goes over the defender.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the start, 1 mark for the throw, 1 mark for going over the defender.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: p means soft. f means loud.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
